title: Portfolio Engine Target Architecture Audit and Roadmap

packages.name: @portfolio-engine/schema
packages.purpose: Shared schemas and validation contracts for config, content, context, and future registry data.

packages.name: @portfolio-engine/engine-core
packages.purpose: Config loading, route injection, virtual modules, override resolution, manifests, and generic runtime contracts.

packages.name: @portfolio-engine/editorial-theme
packages.purpose: The actual site theme: layouts, routes, components, styles, and public editorialTheme(...) API.

packages.name: @portfolio-engine/admin-tools
packages.purpose: Rendered admin/reviewer UI so nontechnical consumers can edit content, config, context, assets, and registry entries without looking at code. Extracted from profesional_site/agreni-site — not a greenfield build.

packages.name: portfolio-engine-workflow-kit
packages.purpose: Local MCP server exposing tools to Claude/Copilot: inspect_site, plan_request, validate_plan, plan_upstream, patch_ledger.

mvpDefinition: v5 defines Backbone MVP (after Phase 3): runtime buildability, consumer layout contract, override bridge when advertised, MVP documentation; workspace-link allowed if docs are clear. Product MVP (after Phase 4): agreni-site and jordan-site as clean private consumers on semver/npm unless an explicit documented exception applies. Registries, admin-tools, workflow-kit, bootstrap, and advanced automation are post–Product-MVP.

productTracks.name: Governance and safety
productTracks.summary: legal, labels, board, contribution safety, docs

mvpMilestones.backboneMvp: After Phase 3 — engine stable: packages build, layout contract proven, MVP docs complete, override bridge if advertised.
mvpMilestones.productMvp: After Phase 4 — agreni-site and jordan-site exist as clean private repos consuming published packages (or documented exception).

phases.title: Planning, governance, and debt visibility
phases.description: Coordinate the v5 audit framing, reconcile the live GitHub board, set the legal and contribution foundation, and standardize the `area:*` and `agent:*` labels that gate AI-assisted work.
phases.motivation: Without an agreed path, a license, governance docs, and machine-readable labels, downstream work duplicates effort and AI contributions become risky. Phase 0 is the prerequisite that lets every other phase proceed with confidence.

phases.title: Runtime backbone buildability
phases.description: Stabilize schema, engine-core, editorial-theme, CI, and Vercel; replace no-op build scripts with real ones so the required packages are actually buildable.
phases.motivation: The runtime is the core product. Without a buildable, type-checked, CI-verified backbone, no consumer can use the engine and no later phase has solid ground.

phases.title: Consumer layout contract, publish, demo migration
phases.description: Define the preferred consumer layout (`src/config`, `src/content`, `src/context`, `src/overrides`, `public`, `.portfolio-engine`), migrate demo-site to it, and publish the first engine packages so agreni-site can consume them via semver.
phases.motivation: The repo layout is the contract for nontechnical site-owners and AI agents. Publishing locks in the boundary between upstream packages and consumer repos so Product MVP can consume real versioned dependencies.

phases.title: Override proof and MVP documentation
phases.description: Land the named override bridge end-to-end (Hero + custom CSS) when overrides are advertised, and ship MVP-level documentation: README, downstream consumption, two-mode docs (workspace vs semver), CONTRIBUTING basics.
phases.motivation: Backbone MVP is both code-stable and documentation-complete. Without override proof and clear consumption docs, consumers cannot adopt the engine and Product MVP cannot be validated.

phases.summary: Engine stable enough to serve real consumer repos. Packages build, layout contract proven, override bridge demonstrated when advertised, MVP docs complete.

phases.title: First consumer products: agreni-site and jordan-site
phases.description: Deliver agreni-site and jordan-site as clean private consumer repos on the target layout, consuming published packages (or documented exception). Migrate or author content/config/context, verify build and preview.
phases.motivation: Two distinct real products at MVP reduce the risk that the backbone only works for one site. Success proves the engine works outside the monorepo.

phases.summary: Two real products (agreni-site + jordan-site) validate the engine end-to-end against the consumer layout contract and published packages.

phases.title: Registries and manifest
phases.description: Move route metadata and supported override surfaces into explicit registries; generate `.portfolio-engine/manifest.json`; ship default registries inside `schema`, `engine-core`, and `editorial-theme`.
phases.motivation: Capabilities are currently implicit (hardcoded route lists, component trees). Explicit registries are machine-readable contracts for agents, admin-tools, and workflow-kit.

phases.title: Admin-tools extraction
phases.description: Extract the existing admin UI from the profesional_site/agreni-site codebase into the `@portfolio-engine/admin-tools` package. Not a greenfield build — most MVP admin features already exist and just need packaging.
phases.motivation: Admin-tools is the intended content editing path for agreni-site (replacing Pages CMS). Extracting first reduces risk of building on top of an unfinished foundation.

phases.title: Consumer extension registry
phases.description: Add the consumer-owned registry as the middle ground between content/config and upstream changes; allow local pages, embeds, and components without editing package internals.
phases.motivation: Consumers should declare local reusable pages and embeds without editing upstream packages or paying the upstream review cost.

phases.title: Python/MCP workflow-kit
phases.description: Build the optional Python package exposing MCP tools to Claude/Copilot: `inspect_site`, `plan_request`, `validate_plan`, `plan_upstream`, `patch_ledger`.
phases.motivation: Consumer agents should not manually run terminal commands or guess repo structure. They should call provider-neutral tools through MCP.

phases.title: Consumer bootstrap and setup
phases.description: Ship a setup script that bootstraps a consumer repo from scratch — required runtime files, optional MCP setup, printed Vercel/GitHub guidance, dry-run support.
phases.motivation: Nontechnical adopters should not have to manually wire a multi-language project. A bootstrap script reduces the barrier to adoption and ensures the layout contract is followed from day one.

phases.title: Demo-site product showcase expansion
phases.description: Build teaching pages on the demo-site that show how config, content, context, overrides, registry, and the MCP workflow-kit work, with rendered result and source snippets side by side.
phases.motivation: Demo-site teaches consumers and agents how to use every layer. Conflating this with the Backbone MVP CI role caused scope creep, so showcase work is deferred until after Product MVP.

phases.title: Contribution safety and admin publishing
phases.description: Add layer-boundary guards, AI review prompts, and public-safe planner workflows for consumer-originated PRs; expose preview/public publishing concepts in admin-tools (branch model, Vercel setup, optional cadence schema).
phases.motivation: Once consumers and their agents start contributing upstream, PRs need to be safe and reviewable. Nontechnical site-owners need clear preview vs production semantics so they don't accidentally publish.
